body:
Fixes #22941
Clause-②: no

One binary replaced in place, nothing else: `apps/docs/public/decks/the-ontology-is-the-software.pdf`, the English deck "The Ontology Is the Software — How a large model reads an enterprise", refreshed from 17 to 19 pages. Same path, so the link at the end of the blog essay (PR #22264) keeps working.

## What changed in the deck

| | Before (PR #22254) | Now |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Pages | 17 | 19 |
| Bytes | 768,057 | 777,904 |
| Opening | cover, then "What is an enterprise?" | cover, then two prologue slides: three interfaces and one user that never changed; a company a few years from now, nine in the morning, ending on "take the people out and switch the systems off, what is left of the enterprise?" |
| Repetition | the five-part definition listed four times; "models change, the ontology stays", "one change, four places" and "written wrong does not ship" each said more than once | each said once; the future table's second column now reads "A few years from now", answering the prologue |

Printed by Chromium (`page.pdf`, one 1920 x 1080 page per slide, `printBackground`) from the slide HTML. Vector text, 26 embedded font objects (Inter, IBM Plex Mono), byline "ObjectStack Team", no speaker name in the text layer.

## Checks

- Docs-site asset only. No `packages/**`, `content/**`, `README.md`, app code or generated ledger. Nothing publishes: `skip-changeset`.
- `scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` judges binary-ness by content and skips real binaries; the PDF is one.
- No model identifier in the PDF text, the commit or this body.
- Seat-executed under the maintainer's instruction quoted on the card ("open a PR"); the seat does not merge its own PR, so this stays a draft for the maintainer to land.
